answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making the task queue itself costly to duplicate: each work order demands a proof-of-work deposit in scarce compute, slashed when peer attestation rejects the result. A thousand puppet accounts then cost a thousand real deposits, since identity is cheap but slashable stake is not. Even in a gale of fake submissions, honest reviewers act as basalt, cross-checking claims against one shared ledger, and a newcomer still finds a haven in a queue that ranks providers by settled history, not account age.
